newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols edge up as bonds slide.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols edge up as bonds slide.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed-income options edged up as underlying markets slid in the afternoon, dealers said.

A slate of economic data due out in the coming weeks, including Tuesday's fourth quarter U.S. employment cost index (ECI) and Friday's gross domestic production (GDP), also kept upward pressure on volatilities, they added.
"For most of the day, volatilities were pretty much unchanged, but the (futures) market has kind of broken down here," said a brokerage Eurodollar trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME).
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options were up a quarter point at around 12.6 and 15.2 percent, respectively.
Traders said the declines in the past few sessions -- most of them coming toward the end of each day -- has made the market look technically fragile.

Even though a majority of the market still did not expect the Fed to raise interest rates at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting Feb 4-5, traders noted that nervousness had been heightened and would keep volatilities well bid going into the ECI and GDP numbers.
"ECI, I think, is the most important because everybody knows that's what (Fed Chairman) Greenspan is looking at," the CME trader said.
Traders said nervousness was likely to persist through Feb 7, when January empolyment report is due.

One of the largest trades in the Eurodollar pit today was a 6,000-contract purchase of soon-expiring February 94.20 puts by an investment bank, a high-gamma play common ahead of important economic figures or events. Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which give the contracts' premiums a sharp acceleration when the underlying market swings.
At the longer end of the yield curve, T-bond volatilities rose as the bond market extened losses in the afternoon.

A bank affiliate trader at Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said that, in addition to the economic numbers and the FOMC meeting, the market was anticipating supply in government and corporate bonds to continue pressuring prices.
CBOT's March Treasury bond futures options rose about a quarter point to 11.2 percent.
